title: Staying back on You Can Depend On Me and Armstrong's Lionel Hampton record
summary: Randolph played the background trumpet softly because Armstrong, remembering how he had held down Lionel Hampton on a Les Hite record, wanted him to stay back.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But getting back to some of the solos, now, for instance, I don't know whether you heard -- did you ever hear the arrangement 'On You can depend on me'?
Do you hear the trumpet in the background?
Yes. That has to be you.
That was me. But, you know what? The engineer was doing this, and Louis was doing this.
The engineer wanted you to play louder and Louis wanted you to play softer, huh?
And, you know, I'm glad that -- you know how I knew to stay back? Otherwise, I wouldn't have
known to stay back. I would have just thought Louis was just doing that, you know.

But when he says, Randy, I'm going to play a record for you. This was down at New Orleans, and he played some record that when he was with Les Hite's band, and Lionel was playing the vibes. And he says, now, you're going to have to listen real hard to hear this, he says, because of the fact, he says, I kept him back. He says, I wish I had let him play out. This is what he told me, now. I'm getting these words from Louis. Now, it's no one can dispute this because the man is dead, but if the man was living, he and I could tell you, he and I was together, alone, and he carried me in his room and played the record. And I could hear -- I just could hear the vibes.

Yeah, it was something. It was really going. And he kept -- he's told me I kept him back. He's says, I wished I had let him play it out. Well, when he would say (musical sounds), and I'd say (musical sounds).

Yeah, it weighed me down. And I knew just what that was, see. I thought about what he said about Lionel, and I stayed down. Didn't bother me, because (unintelligible) all I wanted was (unintelligible).
